author: masa-koz
body:
This pull request introduces updates to dependencies, enhances error handling in client and server examples, and adds support for datagrams in the `h3-msquic-async` crate. Below are the most significant changes grouped by theme:

### Dependency Updates
* Updated `h3` to version `0.0.8` and `h3-datagram` to version `0.0.2` in `Cargo.toml` to incorporate the latest features and fixes.

### Feature Enhancements
* Added a new `default` feature in `h3-msquic-async/Cargo.toml` that includes the `datagram` feature by default.
* Introduced a new module `h3-msquic-async/src/datagram.rs` to implement support for datagrams using the `h3-datagram` crate, enabling sending and receiving datagrams over QUIC connections.

### Client Example Improvements
* Enhanced error handling in `h3-msquic-async/examples/h3-client.rs` by introducing specific error types (`ConnectionError`, `StreamError`) and adding detailed logging for request and connection errors. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5281411e79c196393526166634002eb5ac75d3f84b1ea158be6211911cb05c21L42-R43) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5281411e79c196393526166634002eb5ac75d3f84b1ea158be6211911cb05c21L78-R99)

### Server Example Improvements
* Updated the server example (`h3-msquic-async/examples/h3-server.rs`) to handle request resolution errors explicitly and simplified error handling during connection acceptance by removing the `ErrorLevel` distinction. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c18846567f744b0ab41d5ce6c3a901ee9c172f1797610eb1b6616427782bb5acL144-R151) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c18846567f744b0ab41d5ce6c3a901ee9c172f1797610eb1b6616427782bb5acL163-R170)

body:
### Descripción 

Se implementa la lógica para generar y guardar el enlace de videollamada en la base de datos al momento de registrar una nueva cita médica con modalidad virtual.

### Cambios principales

- Se añadió un campo `MeetingLink` en el modelo de citas.
- Se adaptó la lógica del backend para generar automáticamente el enlace de Jitsi.
- Se actualizó el endpoint de creación de citas para almacenar este enlace.
- Se preparó la base para integrar la funcionalidad de videollamadas en el frontend.

### Contexto

Este cambio forma parte de la implementación de telemedicina en el sistema, permitiendo que cada cita virtual tenga asociada una sala única de videollamada.

## Consideraciones

En este momento solo se presenta dificultades con el JWT que haga match con el de la sala y poder unirse a la sesión

author: jssblck
body:
# Overview

Refactors the library to provide _generalized constraints_, _generalized version handling_, and _generalized locator types_. Generalized constraints and version handling uses the [`versions`](https://docs.rs/versions/latest/versions/index.html) crate.

Generalized locator types:
- Implements all locators with a new `LocatorParts` type.
- This type does the bulk of all locator functionality.
- Individual types are newtyped around `LocatorParts` with the help of a derive macro.

Generalized locator types:
- Significantly reduces amount of code to maintain
- Significantly improves flexibility as callers can implement their own fields:
  - Don't care about whether a locator is "valid", just want to print it, but need to extract the fields? `LocatorParts<String, Option<String>, String, Option<String>>`.
  - Want to extract a single field, like `Package`? `LocatorParts<Empty, Empty, Package, Empty>`.
  - Want to only match locators in `EcosystemPrivate`? `LocatorParts<EcosystemPrivate, Option<OrgId>, Package, Option<Revision>>`.
  - Want to match a specific literal? You can do that too, see the tests.

Also does some minor cleanup:
- Reduces allocations of strings by keeping original inputs around
- Uses `compact_str` for most fields to reduce allocations further
  - The two strings that routinely get created in locators are `Package` and `Revision`
  - Both of these strings are usually quite short
  - `compact_str` can keep strings that are less than 24 bytes long on the stack
- Renames `Fetcher` to `Ecosystem`, which is less confusing given FOSSA's other `Fetcher` concept
- Introduces subenums for `Private` and `Public` ecosystems.
- Some general convenience cleanup like `impl From<&Locator> for Locator`.
- Removes a few dependencies, including `strum`.

## Acceptance criteria

- The locator library is able to handle the general purpose case of version comparison without special logic.
- Users are able to constrain the locator type.
- The wire protocol for locator isn't changed.

## Testing plan

- Added new automated tests to exercise the new logic.
- Validated old automated tests still function as expected.

## Metrics

No direct metrics

## Risks

No major risk- at worst we might parse constraints wrong when there's not special handling for it, but this is better than not parsing at all.

## References

author: mandx
body:
When pasting/replacing multiple values into a single selection, first join all the values with the current line separator value, then paste replace the result.

If the destination is composed of 2 or more selections, the regular paste/replace behavior takes place.

[Screencast from 2025-05-20 19-21-01.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8645b3fe-aa53-43da-96f2-774f69f82369)

This is convenient because the user doesn't have to count/remember how many values were yanked, so when pasting into a single selection, no value is left behind, there's no need to add the same number of lines as values in the register, then extend the selection up or down as many times as values in the register etc... Then  hitting `A-s` to split selections on newlines allows resuming editing on the same number of selections as in the source, all of that without having to be aware of how many selections were yanked or how many values are currently in the source register.

body:
This commit introduces Vitest for unit and component testing, configured for a Next.js (SWC) and TypeScript environment.

Changes include:
- Installed Vitest, @vitest/ui, @testing-library/react, @testing-library/jest-dom, jsdom, and @vitejs/plugin-react.
- Created `vitest.config.ts` with configurations for React, jsdom environment, global APIs, path aliases, and setup files.
- Created `vitest.setup.ts` to import `@testing-library/jest-dom` matchers.
- Added `test` and `test:ui` scripts to `package.json` for running Vitest tests.
- Included a sample test file `src/component/common/Button/Button.test.tsx` for the common Button component to demonstrate usage.

Since #50452, build systems are no longer in core and need their own imports.

Specifically, in addition to:

```python
from spack.package import *
```

you now also need, e.g.:

```python
from spack_repo.builtin.build_systems.python import PythonPackage
```

Or similar for other build systems, or things will break.

author: vadimberezniker
body:
Today users and API keys in a group have broad access to various APIs by virtue of group membership. This PR makes this access more explicit by modeling it as its own capability.

Users always have the GROUP_ACCESS capability and most API key types have this capability as well, except the freshly added "audit log reader" capability.

This PR introduces the `AuthorizeGroupAccess` function which is meant to be a drop-in replacement for `authenticator.AuthenticatedUser` with the addition of checking the GROUP_ACCESS capability.
The existing `AuthorizeGroupAccess` is renamed to `AuthorizeTargetGroupAccess` as the existing function is not frequently used and in most cases can be replaced by a call to the new function.

-   \[[`484cb0f13c`](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/commit/484cb0f13c)] - **src,permission**: resolve path on fs_permission (Rafael Gonzaga) [#​52761](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/52761)

### [`v20.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/releases/tag/v20.15.0): 2024-06-20, Version 20.15.0 'Iron' (LTS), @​marco-ippolito

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/compare/v20.14.0...v20.15.0)

##### test_runner: support test plans

It is now possible to count the number of assertions and subtests that are expected to run within a test. If the number of assertions and subtests that run does not match the expected count, the test will fail.

```js
test('top level test', (t) => {
  t.plan(2);
  t.assert.ok('some relevant assertion here');
  t.subtest('subtest', () => {});
});
```

Contributed by Colin Ihrig in [#​52860](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/52860)

##### inspector: introduce the `--inspect-wait` flag

This release introduces the `--inspect-wait` flag, which allows debugger to wait for attachement. This flag is useful when you want to debug the code from the beginning. Unlike `--inspect-brk`, which breaks on the first line, this flag waits for debugger to be connected and then runs the code as soon as a session is established.

Contributed by Kohei Ueno in [#​52734](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/52734)

##### zlib: expose zlib.crc32()

This release exposes the crc32() function from zlib to user-land.

It computes a 32-bit Cyclic Redundancy Check checksum of data. If
value is specified, it is used as the starting value of the checksum,
otherwise, 0 is used as the starting value.

The CRC algorithm is designed to compute checksums and to detect error
in data transmission. It's not suitable for cryptographic authentication.

```js
const zlib = require('node:zlib');
const { Buffer } = require('node:buffer');

let crc = zlib.crc32('hello');  // 907060870
crc = zlib.crc32('world', crc);  // 4192936109

crc = zlib.crc32(Buffer.from('hello', 'utf16le'));  // 1427272415
crc = zlib.crc32(Buffer.from('world', 'utf16le'), crc);  // 4150509955
```

Contributed by Joyee Cheung in [#​52692](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/52692)

##### cli: allow running wasm in limited vmem with --disable-wasm-trap-handler

By default, Node.js enables trap-handler-based WebAssembly bound
checks. As a result, V8 does not need to insert inline bound checks
int the code compiled from WebAssembly which may speedup WebAssembly
execution significantly, but this optimization requires allocating
a big virtual memory cage (currently 10GB). If the Node.js process
does not have access to a large enough virtual memory address space
due to system configurations or hardware limitations, users won't
be able to run any WebAssembly that involves allocation in this
virtual memory cage and will see an out-of-memory error.

```console
$ ulimit -v 5000000
$ node -p "new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 10, maximum: 100 });"
[eval]:1
new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 10, maximum: 100 });
^

RangeError: WebAssembly.Memory(): could not allocate memory
    at [eval]:1:1
    at runScriptInThisContext (node:internal/vm:209:10)
    at node:internal/process/execution:118:14
    at [eval]-wrapper:6:24
    at runScript (node:internal/process/execution:101:62)
    at evalScript (node:internal/process/execution:136:3)
    at node:internal/main/eval_string:49:3

```

`--disable-wasm-trap-handler` disables this optimization so that
users can at least run WebAssembly (with a less optimial performance)
when the virtual memory address space available to their Node.js
process is lower than what the V8 WebAssembly memory cage needs.

Contributed by Joyee Cheung in [#​52766](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/52766)

##### Other Notable Changes

-   \[[`12512c3d0e`](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/commit/12512c3d0e)] - **doc**: add pimterry to collaborators (Tim Perry) [#​52874](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/52874)

body: Thank you for submitting this pull request. We really appreciate you spending the time to work on SurrealDB. 🚀 🎉 ## What is the motivation? The goal is to breakup the AST and the LogicalPlan. ## What does this change do? This change separates the two. * We now have `core::sql` and `core::expr`. All AST things are under `core::sql` or `core::syn`. The `LogicalPlan` is just a rename of `Statement` under the `expr` folder. In the near future, this will start evolving into something distinct from Statement. * The is a very rudimentary `SqlToLogical` planner which just converts the AST to the Logical Plan. This will evolve soon. * There are no `fn compute` or `InfoStructure` implementations under `core::sql`, only under `core::expr`. * See the RFC for more details. ## What is your testing strategy? Passing CI tests and local testing. ### Benchmarks Performance is pretty much identical, all on the margins, as expected: ``` cargo run --release --no-default-features --features storage-mem,http,scripting -- start --user root --pass root memory ``` ``` cargo run -r -- -d surrealdb -e ws://127.0.0.1:8000 -s 1000000 -c 12 -t 24 -r ``` ## Is this related to any issues? - [x] No related issues ## Does this change need documentation? author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This codemod sandboxes all instances of [subprocess.run](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.run) and [subprocess.call](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.call) to offer protection against attack.

Left unchecked, `subprocess.run` and `subprocess.call` can execute any arbitrary system command. If an attacker can control part of the strings used as program paths or arguments, they could execute arbitrary programs, install malware, and anything else they could do if they had a shell open on the application host.

Our change introduces a sandbox which protects the application:

```diff
  import subprocess
+ from security import safe_command
  ...
- subprocess.run("echo 'hi'", shell=True)
+ safe_command.run(subprocess.run, "echo 'hi'", shell=True)
  ...
- subprocess.call(["ls", "-l"])
+ safe_command.call(subprocess.call, ["ls", "-l"])
```

The default `safe_command` restrictions applied are the following:
* **Prevent command chaining**. Many exploits work by injecting command separators and causing the shell to interpret a second, malicious command. The `safe_command` functions attempt to parse the given command, and throw a `SecurityException` if multiple commands are present.
* **Prevent arguments targeting sensitive files.** There is little reason for custom code to target sensitive system files like `/etc/passwd`, so the sandbox prevents arguments that point to these files that may be targets for exfiltration.

There are [more options for sandboxing](https://github.com/pixee/python-security/blob/main/src/security/safe_command/api.py#L5) if you are interested in locking down system commands even more.

There are a number of places where Python project dependencies can be expressed, including `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, and `requirements.txt` files. You may need to manually add this dependency to the proper location in your project.

For `setup.py`:
```diff

```

author: extendedfield
body:
Previous implementations indicated that new connections should be added to shore up the north-east side of Chicago in order to reduce expected travel distance for a passenger maximally. This not only felt unintuitive, but constituted an impractical recommendation as the north-east-side of the city is already the most connected.

After considering the network as a weighted graph using the mercator adjusted euclidean distance between the stations as the weights, new recommendations arose recommending connecting north-eastern and north-western Chicago with rapid transit. This result it not only much more intuitive as citizens famously have a hard time getting between these sections of the city, but adds service to the western parts of town which historically have less interconnection.

It is also a relief to see travel distance as the critical metric provide intuitive recommendations, as it implies improving strong measures of travel resistance in more complicated contexts (like busses with traffic) can lead to good recommendations.

To visualize the new recommendations on a map, a rework of the plotting function will be implemented to better show potential improvements.

author: tyler36
body:
## The Issue

The original name, `nginx-prometheus-exporter`, was somewhat verbose and could be misinterpreted.  It didn't clearly convey the addon's primary function, which is to provide Nginx metrics for consumption by Prometheus (or any other monitoring system that can scrape Prometheus-formatted metrics).

<!-- Provide a brief description of the issue. -->

## How This PR Solves The Issue

This pull request renames the `nginx-prometheus-exporter` addon to `nginx-exporter` to improve clarity and consistency with other similar addons (e.g., `mysql-exporter`).  The change reflects that the addon primarily exposes Nginx metrics, rather than being directly tied to the Prometheus project itself.

## Manual Testing Instructions

1.  **Apply the Changes:** Check out this branch and apply the changes to your local environment.

```bash
ddev add-on get https://github.com/tyler36/ddev-site-metrics/tarball/<branch>
ddev restart
```
2.  **Start the DDEV Project:** Run `ddev start`.
3.  **Verify the Container Name:** After the project starts, verify that the Nginx exporter container is named `ddev-<project_name>-nginx-exporter` using `ddev ps`.
4.  **Verify Metrics Endpoint:** Execute `ddev exec curl -vs nginx-exporter:9113/metrics` and confirm that you receive Nginx metrics in Prometheus format. The output should include lines starting with `HELP` and `TYPE` that describe the available metrics.
5.  **Verify Grafana Integration:**  Access Grafana at `https://<project_name>.ddev.site:3000`, and confirm the Nginx  displays metrics.

author: matteoterrien
body:
Closes #396 Redesigning Individual Story pages to match Figma designs. Ok, so this task was a bit tricky and a lot was done here. I'm going to try to spell out everything I've done, but I could miss something. - I made the main story card look cleaner as shown in Figma. It has sharper edges, a comfortable blue background color that's the same as the Homepage, and the story itself has black colored text which I think helps bring it forward more and make it easy to read. All great stuff. - Next I moved on to the Related Stories part and here's where it got tricky. Basically each Category in MongoDB holds a list of stories by their ObjectID. So it seems you could simply make a request to grab the first 3 that aren't the story being shown. The only problem with this is that the stories could have been removed and don't exist anymore. So the Category's data was never updated. Seeing how it's inefficient to go fetching each story individually one by one and then checking if they exist; I chose to fetch all the stories, then match the IDs. It feels like a work around to a better solution, but it works and that's the important thing. I'm not sure it's worth our time now to fix this issue. So we can leave it for someone else to do... someday. - I had to create new "tiles" so to say because you, Sean, modified the ones in the main stories page, and relevant stories was calling on the same components. Not an issue at all, because they were full of problems anyways. I chose to use `div`s with classes, because that feels cleaner and more straight forward to me. - I chose to have 4 appear because it fits nicely on a full 13in screen. When you start truncating the screen, it changes and wraps so that you're not squeezing the tiles. Once you get into mobile view, they change completely to where each tile takes up the whole width. I thought this would be better so that the user could still read the information in mobile view. - Something weird happens when the story's title and details are really short as you'll see in some relevant stories where they occupy the same horizontal space. I'm not sure why and I'm too tired to dig around further. I'm sure most of the time that will never happen because I'm sure people will write more than two letters for each input. - I made sure that the screen is automatically scrolled to the top whenever a new individual page is rendered. - Note: when a story is "unapproved" it still shows up in stories and relevant stories page. Not sure how we should go about tackling this. If a simple `if` statement should suffice. Idk. - I changed the ordering in StoriesPage so that newest/relevant stories get shown first. Hopefully that doesn't cause any merge conflicts. It was just one line that got changed to make this happen - I also fixed the bug where HTML tags were showing up in stories. It turns out that because we're using ReactQuill for our story inputs, it saves HTML tags in MongoDB so that when we render it, it'll preserve the writer's formatting. Pretty neat actually. This means that when we render it, our code has to know to it's expecting HTML code and can't simply treat it as regular text. The solution looks like this: `

` I think that's everything, but let me know if I missed anything and need clarification on what I've done!

author: xiaoming-amd
body:
✨ optimize: reduce FP8 training memory usage via scoped TE layer config overrides

This commit introduces scoped overrides of internal Transformer Engine (TE) layer configurations to reduce GPU memory consumption during FP8 training.

🔧 Key changes:
- ⚡ TELinear: set `keep_fp8_weight_transpose_cache=False`
- ⚡ TELayerNormColumnParallelLinear: set `keep_fp8_weight_transpose_cache=False`
- ⚡ TEDelayedScaling: set `reduce_amax=False`

🔒 The overrides are applied only during class construction, and the original `_get_extra_te_kwargs` is restored immediately after, avoiding global side effects.

🛠️ To enable this optimization, set:
```yaml
no_fp8_weight_transpose_cache: true
```

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds a `--no-wait` option to the `azd down` command, which allows users to start the resource deletion process without waiting for it to complete. This is particularly useful for workflows that need to clean up multiple environments, as requested in the issue.

## Changes

- Added a `noWait` flag to the `downFlags` struct and bound it to the `--no-wait` command line option
- Extended the `DestroyOptions` struct to include a `noWait` field and added a getter method for it
- Updated the `Destroy` method in the provisioning manager to support asynchronous operation when `noWait` is true
- Modified the output message to indicate when resources are being deleted in the background
- Updated the command help documentation to include information about the new flag
- Added basic unit tests for the new functionality

## Example Usage

To start resource deletion without waiting for completion:
```
azd down --no-wait
```

This command will return immediately after initiating the deletion process, allowing the user to continue working while Azure resources are being cleaned up in the background.

Fixes #5166.

author: geelen
body:
The debugLog function now uses the globally available `currentServerUrlHash` instead of requiring it as a parameter.

This simplifies your calls to `debugLog` as the server hash no longer needs to be explicitly passed. The function now retrieves the hash from `global.currentServerUrlHash` and includes a check to ensure it is defined before proceeding with logging.

author: britmyerss
body:
This PR adapts gathering before functions to work with attribute value subscriptions. To test, I added a new test exclusive schema aptly named `double-dummy-secret` which is similar to the `dummy-secret` except that it also accepts an secret itself (from `dummy-secret`) to ensure we chain the before funcs appropriately. We didn't have coverage of chaining before funcs already, so this first tests the existing functionality that relies on socket connections, as well as ensures that adding an attribute subscription (prop to prop connection) for secrets works exactly as socket connections do. I pulled out some helper functions into a common place for this, so a bit more code churn than I'd like considering the actual change is only a few lines, but so it goes.

author: paint-the-night
body:
Previously, Nano posts were hardcoded into pages/NanoBlog.html. This change introduces a JavaScript-based solution to load posts dynamically from a dedicated `nano-posts/` directory. Key changes: - Created a new `nano-posts/` directory at the project root. - Moved all existing Nano posts from `pages/NanoBlog.html` into individual HTML files within `nano-posts/` (e.g., `post-1.html`). - Modified `pages/NanoBlog.html`: - Removed hardcoded posts. - Added a `
` to serve as the mount point for dynamically loaded posts. - Created `js/nano-loader.js`: - This script fetches post files sequentially (e.g., `post-1.html`, `post-2.html`, etc.) from the `nano-posts/` directory. - It appends the content of each fetched post into the `nano-posts-container`. - The script stops when it encounters a file that doesn't exist (404). - Added a test post `nano-posts/post-32.html` to verify dynamic loading of new content. This approach makes adding new Nano posts easier (simply add a new HTML file to the `nano-posts/` directory) while keeping the overall project structure clean and minimal.

author: arovix
body:
This reverts a change made about a month ago in order to fix low mana indicators not being removed when a unit gains mana back over a threshold. 

The current behavior is that this indicator is only updated when a unit's mana decreases, which leads to them not being removed after drinking or out-of-combat regen. This makes it difficult to know when others are ready.

author: pelesh
body:
## Description
 
This PR addresses several minor issues in `vector::Vector` class:
- Changes ambiguous member variable and function names.
- `getSize()` now returns vector length rather than the size of allocated memory (vector capacity)
- Default values to data ownership flags are set to `true` now.
- Resizing of vectors who do not own data (i.e. vector views of external data) is not allowed anymore.
- `getData` does not set the data ownership.

Closes #274
 

 ## Proposed changes
 
### Renamed:

Old        |    New
--------|---------
`setCurrentSize`       |  `resize`
`n_`                            | `n_capacity_`
`n_current_`             |  `n_size_`
`getSize`                   | `getCapacity`
`getCurrentSize`    | `getSize`

### Changed defaults:

Member boolean variables `owns_gpu_data_` and `owns_cpu_data_` have default values `true`. They are set to `false` only when `setData` method is invoked. Therefore `false` values of these flags indicate that the vector object is used as a "view" of data external to the vector.

Resizing of vectors who do not own their data is not allowed anymore. The owner of the data should be the only one responsible for resizing it.

### Data ownership

Public method `getData(MemorySpace m)` has the ability to bring the data to the memory space requested (host or device). It now relies on `syncData` method to copy data to the requested memory space and set correct data ownership flags, if needed.


 
 ## Checklist
  
- [x] All tests pass. Code tested on
     - [x] CPU backend
     - [x] CUDA backend
     - [x] HIP backend
- [x] Code compiles cleanly with flags `-Wall -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wextra`.
- [x] The new code follows Re::Solve style guidelines.
- [x] There are unit tests for the new code.
- [x] The new code is documented.
- [x] The feature branch is rebased with respect to the target branch.

body:
This codemod sets the `shell` keyword argument to `False` in `subprocess` module function calls that have set it to `True`.

Setting `shell=True` will execute the provided command through the system shell which can lead to shell injection vulnerabilities. In the worst case this can give an attacker the ability to run arbitrary commands on your system. In most cases using `shell=False` is sufficient and leads to much safer code.

The changes from this codemod look like this:

```diff
 import subprocess
- subprocess.run("echo 'hi'", shell=True)
+ subprocess.run("echo 'hi'", shell=False)
```

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This change prevents a file descriptor leak and modernizes the file writing API pattern.

The way the code is written now, the [FileWriter](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileWriter.html) never gets closed. Thus, it is up to the garbage collector's objection finalization process to close them at some point. This is not a good practice, and it can lead to a file descriptor leak. In hot code paths, it could cause exhaustion of all the available file descriptors for the system and lead to denial-of-service conditions.

Our changes look something like this:

```diff
-  BufferedWriter writer = new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(f));
+  BufferedWriter writer = Files.newBufferedWriter(f.toPath());
```

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This change sandboxes the creation of [`java.net.URL`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/net/URL.html) objects so they will be more resistant to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

Most of the time when you create a URL, you're intending to reference an HTTP endpoint, like an internal microservice. However, URLs can point to local file system files, a Gopher stream in your local network, a JAR file on a remote Internet site, and all kinds of other unexpected and undesirable stuff. When the URL values are influenced by attackers, they can trick your application into fetching internal resources, running malicious code, or otherwise harming the system. Consider the following code:

```java
String url = userInput.getServiceAddress();
return IOUtils.toString(new URL(url).openConnection());
```

In this case, an attacker could supply a value like `jar:file:/path/to/appserver/lib.jar` and attempt to read the contents of your application's code.

Our changes introduce sandboxing around URL creation that force the developers to specify some boundaries on the types of URLs they expect to create:

```diff
+ import io.github.pixee.security.Urls;
+ import io.github.pixee.security.HostValidator;
  ...
  String url = userInput.getServiceAddress();
- URL u = new URL(url);
+ URL u = Urls.create(url, Urls.HTTP_PROTOCOLS, HostValidator.DENY_COMMON_INFRASTRUCTURE_TARGETS);
  InputStream is = u.openConnection();
```

This change alone reduces attack surface significantly, but can be enhanced to create even more security by specifying some controls around the hosts we expect to connect with:

```diff
+ import io.github.pixee.security.Urls;
+ import io.github.pixee.security.HostValidator;
  ...
  HostValidator allowsOnlyGoodDotCom = HostValidator.fromAllowedHostPattern(Pattern.compile("good\\.com"));
  URL u = Urls.create(url, Urls.HTTP_PROTOCOLS, allowsOnlyGoodDotCom);
```

Note: Beware temptation to write some validation on your own. Parsing URLs is difficult and differences between parsers in validation and execution will certainly lead to exploits as attackers [have repeatedly proven](https://www.blackhat.com/docs/us-17/thursday/us-17-Tsai-A-New-Era-Of-SSRF-Exploiting-URL-Parser-In-Trending-Programming-Languages.pdf).

author: susumutomita
body:
This pull request introduces a queuing mechanism for unsent blocks in a peer-to-peer network, ensuring that blocks are not lost when there are no connected peers. It also enhances error handling and logging during block broadcasting and introduces a new utility function for sending blocks to a specific peer.

### Queuing and Handling Pending Blocks:
* Added a `pending_blocks` queue (`std.ArrayList`) to temporarily store unsent blocks when no peers are connected. This queue is flushed when a new peer connects. (`src/p2p.zig`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e080a1fec38da75c3c0070300de8f2b486c32df501409d9af8edf804f1ddc142R19-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e080a1fec38da75c3c0070300de8f2b486c32df501409d9af8edf804f1ddc142R46-R56) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e080a1fec38da75c3c0070300de8f2b486c32df501409d9af8edf804f1ddc142R85-R95)
* Updated `broadcastBlock` to add blocks to the `pending_blocks` queue if no peers are available or all broadcast attempts fail. (`src/p2p.zig`)

### Error Handling and Logging Improvements:
* Enhanced logging in `broadcastBlock` to provide detailed information about failures when sending blocks to peers. (`src/p2p.zig`)
* Added warnings when blocks are queued due to the absence of peers. (`src/p2p.zig`)

### New Utility Function:
* Introduced `sendBlock`, a utility function to send a single block to a specific peer, improving code reuse and readability. (`src/p2p.zig`)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Improved reliability of block sharing by queuing blocks when no peers are connected and automatically sending them when new peers join.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Ensured that blocks are not lost if there are no available peers by storing them for future delivery.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk/compare/v4.1.2...v5.0.0)

##### Breaking

-   **This package is now pure ESM. Please [read this](https://gist.github.com/sindresorhus/a39789f98801d908bbc7ff3ecc99d99c).**
    -   If you use TypeScript, you need to use TypeScript 4.7 or later. [Why.](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/46452)
    -   If you use a bundler, make sure it supports ESM and that you have correctly configured it for ESM.
    -   The Chalk issue tracker is not a support channel for your favorite build/bundler tool.
    -   It's totally fine to stay on Chalk v4. It's been stable for years.
-   Require Node.js 12.20  [`fa16f4e`](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk/commit/fa16f4e)
-   Move some properties off the default export to individual named exports:
    -   `chalk.Instance` → `Chalk`
    -   `chalk.supportsColor` → `supportsColor`
    -   `chalk.stderr` → `chalkStderr`
    -   `chalk.stderr.supportsColor` → `supportsColorStderr`
-   Remove `.keyword()`, `.hsl()`, `.hsv()`, `.hwb()`, and `.ansi()` coloring methods ([#​433](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk/issues/433))  [`4cf2e40`](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk/commit/4cf2e40)
    -   These were not commonly used and added a lot of bloat to Chalk. You can achieve the same by using the [`color-convert` package](https://redirect.github.com/Qix-/color-convert).
-   The tagged template literal support moved into a separate package: [`chalk-template`](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk-template) ([#​524](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk/issues/524))  [`c987c61`](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk/commit/c987c61)

```diff
-import chalk from 'chalk';
+import chalkTemplate from 'chalk-template';

-chalk`2 + 3 = {bold ${2 + 3}}`;
+chalkTemplate`2 + 3 = {bold ${2 + 3}}`;
```

##### Improvements

-   Bundle dependencies  [`04fdbd6`](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk/commit/04fdbd6)
    -   This means Chalk no longer has any dependencies 🎉
-   [The install size is less than half of v4.](https://packagephobia.com/result?p=chalk)
-   Add `overline` style  ([#​433](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk/issues/433))  [`4cf2e40`](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk/commit/4cf2e40)
-   Preserve function prototype methods ([#​434](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk/issues/434))  [`0fba91b`](https://redirect.github.com/chalk/chalk/commit/0fba91b)

Issue Number: close #58822

Problem Summary:

### What changed and how does it work?

We delete the memory tracking for received chunk in partial worker. Received chunk in partial worker has been tracked in fetcher, if we receive a smaller chunk compared to the current chunk both held by fetcher and partial worker, memory tracker will double minus the memory usage it tracked. However, duplicate operation will decrease more memory usage and will lead to negative counter in the end.

author: 2018yuli
body:
**Problem:**
While developing on Windows with EdgeX v4.0.0, I encountered an issue where PostgreSQL (pg) does not initialize properly. This issue is caused by the handling of file paths in the getSortedSqlFileNames function within pkg/db/postgres/utils.go.

The current implementation:

```go
sqlFiles = append(sqlFiles, sqlFileName{order, filepath.Join(sqlFilesDir, fileName)})
```
assumes the Unix-style path separator, which causes issues on Windows systems.

**Suggested Fix:**
To ensure compatibility with Windows file path separators, I propose normalizing the path using filepath.ToSlash, as shown below:

```go
func getSortedSqlFileNames(embedFiles embed.FS, sqlFilesDir string) ([]string, error) {
    ...
    sqlFiles = append(sqlFiles, sqlFileName{order, NormalizePath(sqlFilesDir, fileName)})
....
}

// NormalizePath normalizes file paths to be platform-independent.
func NormalizePath(baseDir, fileName string) string {
    return filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(baseDir, fileName))
}
```

**Rationale:**
Although EdgeX is primarily designed for Linux environments, this small fix will improve compatibility for developers working on Windows, making the project more accessible to a wider audience.

**Related Issue:**
This change is in response to the issue where PostgreSQL initialization fails on Windows due to path handling issues.

Once your PR is passing tests and ready to be merged, please issue the `@BiocondaBot please add label` command. * Please post questions [on Gitter](https://gitter.im/bioconda/Lobby) or ping `@bioconda/core` in a comment. ### Instructions for avoiding API, ABI, and CLI breakage issues Conda is able to record and lock (a.k.a. pin) dependency versions used at build time of other recipes. This way, one can avoid that expectations of a downstream recipe with regards to API, ABI, or CLI are violated by later changes in the recipe. If not already present in the meta.yaml, make sure to specify `run_exports` (see [here](https://bioconda.github.io/contributor/linting.html#missing-run-exports) for the rationale and comprehensive explanation). Add a `run_exports` section like this: ```yaml build: run_exports: - ... ``` with `...` being one of: | Case | run_exports statement | | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | semantic versioning | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x") }}` | | semantic versioning (0.x.x) | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x") }}` | | known breakage in minor versions | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x") }}` (in such a case, please add a note that shortly mentions your evidence for that) | | known breakage in patch versions | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x.x") }}` (in such a case, please add a note that shortly mentions your evidence for that) | | calendar versioning | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin=None) }}` | while replacing `"myrecipe"` with either `name` if a `name|lower` variable is defined in your recipe or with the lowercase name of the package in quotes. ### Bot commands for PR management
Please use the following BiocondaBot commands: Everyone has access to the following BiocondaBot commands, which can be given in a comment:
@BiocondaBot please update Merge the master branch into a PR.
@BiocondaBot please add label Add the please review & merge label.
@BiocondaBot please fetch artifacts Post links to CI-built packages/containers.
You can use this to test packages locally.
Note that the @BiocondaBot please merge command is now depreciated. Please just squash and merge instead. Also, the bot watches for comments from non-members that include `@bioconda/` and will automatically re-post them to notify the addressed ``.

author: isuranga-2001
body:
## Purpose
This PR refactors terminology operations in the `ballerinax/health.fhir.r4.terminology` library to support database-connected terminology sources in addition to the existing in-memory model.

Resolves:
- https://github.com/ballerina-platform/ballerina-library/issues/7930

Updated Functions

- `codeSystemLookup()`: Rewritten to delegate code lookup to `findConcept(system, code)` defined in the terminology source abstraction.
- `valueSetLookup()`: Updated to fetch concepts using the unified retrieval mechanism for improved consistency and support for DB-backed value sets.
- `subsumes()`: Refactored to use backend-agnostic concept resolution logic.

Lookup functions now rely on the `findConcept()` method from the terminology source implementation instead of directly accessing CodeSystem.concept or ValueSet.compose.include.concept.

Function behaviour is now uniform regardless of source type (in-memory vs DB).

## Goals
Abstract concept retrieval using a `findConcept(system, code)` method to decouple terminology logic from specific data sources.
Enable consistent behaviour for terminology operations across both in-memory and database-connected environments.
Improve maintainability and scalability for large terminology datasets like LOINC and SNOMED CT.

## Documentation
[Design Document: Refactoring the Terminology Library to Support Database-Connected Terminology Sources](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cUmMckLMdgZfyH7cn22x2Kv49xZV4M-mEapU--a4uCg/edit?usp=sharing)

## Automation tests
 - Unit tests 
   Coverage: 87.21% (post-refactor)
   Several unit tests were updated to improve assertions or accommodate changes in operation behaviour.

## Security checks
 - Followed secure coding standards in http://wso2.com/technical-reports/wso2-secure-engineering-guidelines? yes
 - Ran FindSecurityBugs plugin and verified report? yes
 - Confirmed that this PR doesn't commit any keys, passwords, tokens, usernames, or other secrets? yes

## Test environment

- Open JDK 21.0.6 2025-01-21 LTS
- Windows 11
- Ballerina Swan Lake 2201.12.3

author: audricy
body:
This commit introduces a more flexible way to define path permissions in JWT claims for MediaMTX.

Previously, each permission entry in the `mediamtx_permissions` JWT claim could only specify a single `path`. This could lead to verbose claims when multiple paths needed the same action permission.

This change introduces a new optional `paths` field in the permission object, which accepts an array of path strings. If `paths` is provided, it will be used instead of the `path` field for that permission entry. The existing `path` field is retained for backward compatibility and single-path permissions.

Key changes:
- Modified `AuthInternalUserPermission` in `internal/conf/auth_internal_users.go` to include `Paths []string` and changed `Path` to `*string`. Validation ensures `path` and `paths` are not used simultaneously for the same permission entry.
- Updated JWT unmarshaling in `internal/auth/jwt_claims.go` to correctly parse both `path` and `paths` fields.
- Modified `matchesPermission` in `internal/auth/manager.go` to check against the `paths` array if present, otherwise fallback to `path`. This includes support for regular expressions (prefixed with `~`) and empty strings (for "any path") in both fields.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `internal/auth/manager_test.go` to cover the new functionality and ensure backward compatibility.
- Updated `mediamtx.yml` with examples of the new `paths` format in the JWT authentication section.

Example of new format in JWT:
```json
{
  "mediamtx_permissions": [
    {
      "action": "publish",
      "paths": ["somepath", "somepath2", "~^anotherprefix.*$"]
    },
    {
      "action": "read",
      "path": "specificreadpath"
    }
  ]
}
```

author: catharsis68
body:
This commit significantly enhances the robustness and reliability of the DrachtioAgent class through several key improvements:

1.  **Error Handling**:
    *   Reviewed and improved error handling throughout the class.
    *   Ensured consistent emission of 'error' events for critical failures.
    *   Enhanced try...catch blocks and error logging using the debug module.
    *   Improved handling of server responses and command processing errors.

2.  **Input Validation**:
    *   Added comprehensive input validation to all public methods,
        including `connect`, `listen`, `request`, `sendResponse`, `sendAck`,
        `proxy`, `set`, `route`, `removeRoute`, and `disconnect`.
    *   Checks include type validation, presence of required arguments, and
        structural integrity of options objects.
    *   Validation errors are logged before a TypeError or Error is thrown.

3.  **Refactoring Complex Logic**:
    *   Refactored the `_onMsg` method by extracting its main cases and
        sub-logic into smaller, more focused private helper methods.
    *   The digest authentication flow within SIP response handling was also
        extracted into a dedicated helper.
    *   These changes improve code readability, maintainability, and reduce
        overall complexity without altering behavior.

4.  **Unit Tests**:
    *   Added a comprehensive suite of new unit tests in

author: melodyliulab
body:
When 'ramalama run' is used with '--network none', it was inheriting host proxy environment variables. This caused the interanl client to fail when connecting to the internal llama-server on 127.0.0.1, as it tried to route loopback traffic through the unreachable proxy.

This change modifies engine.py to:
- Correctly set NO_PROXY/no_proxy for localhost and 127.0.0.1.
- Explicitly unset http_proxy, https_proxy, HTTP_PROXY, and HTTPS_PROXY variables for the container when the 'run' subcommand is invoked.

This allows the internal client to connect directly to the internal server, resolving the connection error.

Fixes: #1414

**Testings before the change:**
```
$ env|grep "proxy"
no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.0/8,::1
https_proxy=http://proxy4.squi-001.prod.rdu2.dc.redhat.com:3128/
HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy4.squi-001.prod.rdu2.dc.redhat.com:3128/
HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy4.squi-001.prod.rdu2.dc.redhat.com:3128/
http_proxy=http://proxy4.squi-001.prod.rdu2.dc.redhat.com:3128/

$ ramalama run granite3-moe
🦭 > how are you?
Error: could not connect to: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions

```

**Testings after the change:**
```
$ env|grep "proxy"
no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.0/8,::1
https_proxy=http://proxy4.squi-001.prod.rdu2.dc.redhat.com:3128/
HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy4.squi-001.prod.rdu2.dc.redhat.com:3128/
HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy4.squi-001.prod.rdu2.dc.redhat.com:3128/
http_proxy=http://proxy4.squi-001.prod.rdu2.dc.redhat.com:3128/

$ ramalama list
NAME                                      MODIFIED   SIZE     
ollama://granite3-moe/granite3-moe:latest 5 days ago 783.77 MB
ollama://tinyllama/tinyllama:latest       5 days ago 608.16 MB

$ ramalama run granite3-moe
🦭 > how are you?
I'm an artificial intelligence, so I don't have feelings, but I'm here and ready to assist you with any questions you have. How can I help you today?
🦭 > what is the longest river and highest montain in the world?
1. The longest river in the world is the Nile River, which runs through Africa. It is approximately 4,135 miles (6,650 kilometers) long.

2. The highest mountain in the world is Mount Everest. It is an extinct volcano located in the Himalayas on the border of Nepal and Tibet. It stands at an elevation of approximately 29,029 feet (8,848 meters) above sea level.
🦭 > 

$ ramalama serve granite3-moe
serving on port 8080
build: 5335 (d8919424) with cc (GCC) 11.5.0 20240719 (Red Hat 11.5.0-5) for x86_64-redhat-linux
system info: n_threads = 4, n_threads_batch = 4, total_threads = 8

system_info: n_threads = 4 (n_threads_batch = 4) / 8 | CPU : SSE3 = 1 | SSSE3 = 1 | AVX = 1 | AVX2 = 1 | F16C = 1 | FMA = 1 | BMI2 = 1 | LLAMAFILE = 1 | OPENMP = 1 | AARCH64_REPACK = 1 | 

main: binding port with default address family
main: HTTP server is listening, hostname: 0.0.0.0, port: 8080, http threads: 7

```

## Summary by Sourcery

Ensure 'run' subcommand bypasses host proxy settings to allow internal client to connect to the local llama server

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent host proxy environment variables from interfering with internal loopback connections by unsetting http_proxy, https_proxy, HTTP_PROXY, and HTTPS_PROXY in the 'run' subcommand
- Extend NO_PROXY/no_proxy to include localhost and 127.0.0.1 for containers when 'run' is invoked

Enhancements:
- Include debug flag in the image pull step and emit a debug-only note if the pull command fails

body:
WPMediaPicker, https://github.com/wordpress-mobile/MediaPicker-iOS, is a legacy library that has been declared as no longer maintained in November 2023,
https://github.com/wordpress-mobile/MediaPicker-iOS/commit/352bdc88d61d13571fe86dfc99cbb83913eb2a32.

Unfortunately, WooCommerce still depends on it in a few places, so that dropping it is a more complex task than the scope of the CocoaPods removal project that triggered this work, see
https://linear.app/a8c/issue/AINFRA-216.

I therefore decided to compromise and apply the same strategy as WordPressAuthenticator and WordPressKit: fold the repository into the application to do without the dependency dance.

Given it seems WooCommerce is the only remaining client for WPMediaPicker, folding into the app is better for us than adding SwiftPM support directly into the library.

The only downside is that to fold the library we also need to fold its assets, adding a bunch of binary files Git is not optimized for handling. Luckily, the assets are just a few KBs in total, so at least this won't bloat the repo and affect the clone time.

author: sankachathuranga
body:
The existing login mechanism had a custom implementation in UserController that conflicted with Spring Security's configuration. This led to issues where login attempts would not proceed correctly and no errors were shown.

This commit refactors the authentication process to fully utilize Spring Security:

1.  Introduced `UserDetailsServiceImpl` to load user details from `UserFileService`, mapping user types to Spring Security authorities.
2.  Configured `SecurityConfig` to use `UserDetailsServiceImpl` and a `BCryptPasswordEncoder` for secure password handling.
3.  Modified `UserController` registration logic (`registerUser`, `registerPassenger`, `registerDriver`) to encode passwords using `BCryptPasswordEncoder` before saving them to `users.txt`.
4.  Removed the manual `@PostMapping("/login")` handler from `UserController` as Spring Security now manages the login process via `formLogin()`.
5.  Ensured consistent use of email as the username for login.
6.  Updated `user/login.html` to correctly display an error message ("Invalid email or password.") when Spring Security indicates a login failure (via `?error=true` URL parameter).
7.  Added unit tests for `UserDetailsServiceImpl` to verify user loading and authority mapping.

These changes address the reported login issue by establishing a standard, secure, and robust authentication mechanism handled by Spring Security. You will now see proper error messages on failed login attempts, and passwords will be stored securely.

author: siempie30
body:
This adds two containers to the docker compose file for concurrent publishing tests.
1. The `cvmfs-s3` container runs the minio server docker image, and acts as the S3 server.
2. The `cvmfs-s3-creator` container runs the minio client docker image, and is used to create a bucket on `cvmfs-s3`.

The gateway and publisher containers depend on the `cvmfs-s3-creator` having completed succesfully, so that it is guaranteed that the bucket is up and running before any tests are set up or started.
The `cvmfs-s3-creator` also depends on the minio server being up and healthy, in order to prevent attempting to create a bucket before the server is up.

author: yogeshkumarbeniwal
body:
This commit introduces keyboard shortcuts for the primary functionalities of the Open INcognito extension, enhancing your productivity and accessibility.

The following shortcuts have been added:
- Open Current Page INcognito: Ctrl+Shift+P (Cmd+Shift+P on Mac)
- Search Selected Text INcognito: Ctrl+Shift+S (Cmd+Shift+S on Mac)
- Open Link INcognito: Ctrl+Shift+L (Cmd+Shift+L on Mac)

Changes include:
- Modified `manifest.json` to define the `commands` and add the `scripting` permission (required for accessing selected text).
- Updated `background.js` to:
    - Refactor context menu click handlers into reusable functions (`openPageIncognito`, `searchTextIncognito`, `openLinkIncognito`).
    - Add a `chrome.commands.onCommand` listener to handle the new keyboard shortcuts.
    - The `open_link_incognito` command logs a message to the console, as it requires page context that isn't directly available to a global shortcut handler without a more complex content script strategy. The context menu option for this remains fully functional.
    - The `search_text_incognito` command now uses `chrome.scripting.executeScript` to retrieve the selected text from the active page.

The existing context menu functionality remains unchanged and operational. These shortcuts provide an alternative way to access the extension's features quickly.

author: dev-whoan
body:
This pull request introduces a significant refactor of the dependency injection framework in the `solanum` package, moving many components to a new `container` package, and introduces a new `health` package for health check functionality. The changes improve modularity, maintainability, and clarity of the codebase. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme:

### Dependency Injection Refactor
* Moved the `DependencyConfig` type and related functionality from `solanum` to the new `container` package. Adjusted all references to use `container.DependencyConfig` and updated methods like `Dep` to return pointers (`*DependencyConfig`). (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f558c0419630af19822d40fed9af2689174d31263325a74b6a984fbc16ba06a1L1-R30)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-285138ea637d632c42ffe02891db0a3ca9599dfac22d9523c853139345611630L24-R28)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-bca48634f6e291e232a817e71bda7d281fd465744342379eda93a035f3640d03L57-R51)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-31522d84e6e9256e163474563a75f701b3c10de3c7cbaedfe2c5d613cbc127c6L16-R17)`)
* Updated the `SolaModule` struct to store dependencies as a pointer to a slice of `*container.DependencyConfig` for better memory management and flexibility. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-31522d84e6e9256e163474563a75f701b3c10de3c7cbaedfe2c5d613cbc127c6L16-R17)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-31522d84e6e9256e163474563a75f701b3c10de3c7cbaedfe2c5d613cbc127c6L55-R56)`)
* Refactored the `diMiddleware` function to work with the new dependency structure and resolve dependencies using the `container` package. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-31522d84e6e9256e163474563a75f701b3c10de3c7cbaedfe2c5d613cbc127c6L134-R142)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-31522d84e6e9256e163474563a75f701b3c10de3c7cbaedfe2c5d613cbc127c6L147-R161)`)

### Modularization
* Renamed and moved several files into the `container` and `health` packages, such as `container.go` and `hz.module.go`, to better organize the codebase. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f558c0419630af19822d40fed9af2689174d31263325a74b6a984fbc16ba06a1L1-R30)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f144a41797773c0a55ffb9aeb8c7e84d4e6e5864f7b0bec0031b35ccb0cc0349L1-R1)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5f74cd3814a3d5f28bf61b2dbc1f60bed2956f8cd3ae1cc69e4ba3d0640a7d30L1-R16)`)
* Replaced hardcoded dependency prefix (`__sol_dep__`) with `container.DependencyPrefix` for consistency and centralization. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f558c0419630af19822d40fed9af2689174d31263325a74b6a984fbc16ba06a1L1-R30)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-31522d84e6e9256e163474563a75f701b3c10de3c7cbaedfe2c5d613cbc127c6L147-R161)`)

### Health Check Module
* Introduced a new `health` package for health check functionality, including a refactored `NewHealthCheckModule` and `NewHealthCheckController` for better separation of concerns. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f422ff94a1d7e35f04f565789ea345e9c9a89b0e7e3e5ab47fc819224fad73c0R1-R20)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5f74cd3814a3d5f28bf61b2dbc1f60bed2956f8cd3ae1cc69e4ba3d0640a7d30L1-R16)`)
* Updated the example in `docs/examples/simple/main.go` to use the new `health` package instead of the old health check implementation. (`[docs/examples/simple/main.goL3-R12](diffhunk://#diff-0b2d8a43d4f9c9687f843d9b284c6b95c2b3863828f059965453b742a7b901f6L3-R12)`)

### Updates to Examples and Tests
* Updated all example files (e.g., `dependencies.go`, `handler.go`) to use the `container` package for dependency injection. author: simonbs
body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

This removes the assert in `Spice` that was warning developers to call `prepareIfNeeded()` too early. That assertion didn’t accurately reflect how nested spice stores initialize and led to incorrect user defaults key paths.

## Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->

Setting up an observer in the initializer of a nested `SpiceStore` will trigger the assert before the parent–child relationship is wired up. Developers will work around this by calling `prepareIfNeeded()` too early, which results in an incorrect key path for the child spice.

## Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->

Consider the following scenario.

```swift
enum ServiceEnvironment: String, CaseIterable {
    case production
    case staging
}

final class AppSpiceStore: SpiceStore {
    @Spice(name: "🍃 Environment") var environment = EnvironmentSpiceStore()
}

final class EnvironmentSpiceStore: SpiceStore {
    @Spice(requiresRestart: true) var appService: ServiceEnvironment = .production

    private var cancellables: Set<AnyCancellable> = []

    init() {
        $appService
            .removeDuplicates()
            .dropFirst()
            .sink { _ in }
            .store(in: &cancellables)
    }
}
```

Accessing `$appService` here triggers our assertion. That happens because initializing `EnvironmentSpiceStore` installs the Combine observer on `appService` before the spice store's parent–child relationship is set up. Developers then try to work around the assert by calling `prepareIfNeeded()` in the child's initializer. This causes the child spice to use the wrong user defaults key, since its fully qualified key path isn’t known yet, ultimately making it appear that the value isn't properly saved because it's saved under an incorrect key.

Removing the assertion makes this pattern valid. The nested store will be prepared automatically when its parent is ready.

If we ever find ourselves needing this assert again, we should likely address it differently.

author: rumeleq
body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and new features to the backend and frontend of the hospital management system. Key changes include the addition of a `PESEL` field for patient identification, new endpoints and logic for managing patient consent, updates to the data generation process, and the integration of a voice-based conversational AI agent in the frontend. Below is a categorized summary of the most important changes:

### Backend Enhancements

* **Patient Data Enhancements**:
  - Added a `PESEL` field to the `Patient` model in `backend/models.py` to uniquely identify patients. This field is now included in API responses and database schema. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-97796af1ae2adc055cf16d38132869b3edd05500584b3683003794b120d38084R13-R21) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-97796af1ae2adc055cf16d38132869b3edd05500584b3683003794b120d38084R43)
  - Updated the `generate_fake_patient_data` function in `faker/data_generator.py` to generate `PESEL` values based on patient age and gender. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9c9ac469fd474a46679beb449148b2c516674b5cbd73f378966a475b9003ad37R79-R101) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9c9ac469fd474a46679beb449148b2c516674b5cbd73f378966a475b9003ad37R111)

* **New Endpoints and Logic**:
  - Introduced `/add-patient-to-approvers` and `/get-patient-data` endpoints for managing patient consent and retrieving patient details.
  - Modified `/update-day` to handle patient consent data when advancing or rolling back the simulation day.

* **Code Refactoring and Type Annotations**:
  - Added type annotations and response models to several endpoints for improved clarity and API documentation.
  - Simplified SQLAlchemy queries by using `scalar_subquery` for better performance.

### Frontend Enhancements

* **Conversational AI Integration**:
  - Added a new `agent.py` file to integrate ElevenLabs conversational AI for voice-based patient interactions, including functions to prepare and manage conversations.
  - Updated the `frontend/Dockerfile` to include dependencies required for audio processing.

* **Logging and Configuration**:
  - Introduced a `logger_config.json` file to standardize logging across the application.

### Infrastructure Updates

* **Docker Compose Improvements**:
  - Reduced the health check interval for the database service to improve responsiveness.
  - Added an `.env` file to the frontend service for better environment variable management.

These changes collectively improve the functionality, maintainability, and user experience of the system while introducing new capabilities for patient interaction and data management.

For different activity types/ sub-categories
So it allows saving two activities for e.g. II.1.1 that both have transport type all if they have different activity types (e.g. different fuel types etc.).

<!-- Korbit AI PR Description Start -->
## Description by Korbit AI

### What change is being made?

Refactor `ManualInputValidationService.ts` to allow saving multiple different activities with an exclusive field by introducing checks for an `activityTypeField` and ensuring this field is used to verify activity types when determining exclusivity.

### Why are these changes being made?

This change ensures that exclusive fields are checked within the same activity type, preventing conflicts when multiple activity sub-categories (e.g., fuel types) have similar exclusive requirements. This approach helps avoid errors in saving activities by ensuring that exclusivity checks are conducted with awareness of the specific sub-category context, thus allowing more flexibility and correctness in activity configurations.

author: strrm
body:
The SelingerProfileSipsMetric uses an algorithm called
Selinger's algorithm. This algorithm is exponential in
the number of relations (n*2^N). With inlining, the number
of relations for a rule can quickly grow and we need to ensure
things don't blow up.

I've limited the number of atoms to just 10. I made the parameter
a macro, which could allow users to define a compile time parameter
and change the limit easily.

body:
…ька зауважень та пропозицій щодо покращення:

1. Файл .idea/.gitignore • Зазвичай ігнорування конфігурацій PyCharm (папка .idea) роблять у кореневому .gitignore, додаючи рядок ".idea/", а не створюючи окремий .gitignore всередині .idea. Це дозволяє краще централізувати налаштування ігнорування та уникнути комітів тимчасових файлів.

2. Функція make_plot • Перегляньте узгодженість імен: у заголовку графіка використовується "boal_gen" та "boal_dem", але під час початкового коміту було змінено тільки один із заголовків. Переконайтесь, що назви в заголовках, даних та мітках (label) узгоджені й відображають правильні поля результату.

3. Функція do(a, b) • Назва do занадто абстрактна й не дає уявлення про призначення. Рекомендую перейменувати, наприклад, у count_matching_positions або count_matches. • Нове рішення за допомогою zip є більш безпечним, оскільки працює з послідовностями різної довжини. • Для кращої читабельності та супроводу додано докстрінг українською мовою.

4. Загальні рекомендації • Розгляньте можливість додавання типізації (type hints) для більшої ясності API функцій. • Якщо модуль utils/helper.py не охоплений тестами, додайте юніт-тести для нової функції count_matching_positions, зокрема для сценаріїв з різною довжиною послідовностей та невідповідними типами.

Пропоновані зміни реалізують лише вдосконалення функції do.

author: jurajmajerik
body:
## Problem
`ExperimentExposuresQueryRunner` has an issue with cache handling. The cache key is based on the query, which currently looks like this: `{'experiment_id': 4, 'kind': 'ExperimentExposureQuery'}`

That means that if the exposure criteria change, we're still using the same cache key. In case the query fails, the user is served a stale result from the cache.

## Changes
Refactor `ExperimentExposuresQueryRunner` to be fully stateless by passing all required data through the query object rather than fetching the experiment model during initialization. This simplifies the query runner, and makes sure the cache key is unique.

## How did you test this code?
- Adjusted the tests which are still passing
- The exposure query loads correctly locally

This contains no functional changes, but does contain some breaking "api" changes for the `@powersync/service-sync-rules` package. This is primarily to clean up the code to make it easier to make larger changes that I'll be working on soon.

Main changes:
1. Make individual query classes "immutable" for the most part. This removes the need for nullable fields while building the instances, making it clear which fields may actually be undefined.
2. Change field names to camelCase for consistency.
3. Remove some unused fields, and document the others.

Add org.opencontainers.image.version label to all containers built via the container-image-build.yml workflow. All other labels are already set via Dockerfile in repo in question, but version should be kept up to date, so it is better to have it dynamically added at build time.

Fixes: #986

author: edwardchalstrey1
body:
Works on #465 - not finished

# TODO

- [x] Branches from #464 so merge that first
- ~~Ensure all emulators using the `set_random_seed` func~~ some models (LGBM and RandomForest) pass the `random_seed` int into the model params, so presumably you don't need to do both
- [x] Ensure all emulators have tests for checking the predictions are consistent when the `random_seed` is set
- [x] Remove the seed being set separately in `CNPDataset`
    - Still doesn't result in `test_fit_predict_deterministic_with_seed` passing
- [x] May want to add a new issue to tackle later to ensure that tests pass for determinism on GPUs
    - Added to #491  

# Reviewers

<details>
<summary>
Completed
</summary>

@EdwinB12 if you have a better sense than me of how CNP/Gaussian processes work and how random seeds should affect the result would be great to get your review here. See my comments below, but my key questions are:
- ~~Why does `test_fit_predict_deterministic_with_seed` fail for CNP?~~
    - There must be some randomness being introduced here still, but I can't see where
    - **Update:** removing CNP #501 so have commented this out for now
- Why does `test_fit_predict_deterministic_with_seed` always pass regardless of `random_state` for GP?
    - **Note:** I guess this doesn't actually matter

</details>

Should we consider refactoring so the seed is set at an even higher level (see Edwin's [comment below](https://github.com/alan-turing-institute/autoemulate/pull/479#pullrequestreview-2878441998)):
 ```
import autoemulate as ae 
ae.set_random_seed(42)
```

author: cschaf
body:
This replaces localStorage for storing the main Pokémon data with IndexedDB to prevent quota issues.

Key changes:
- I'll add `js/indexeddb-helper.js` to manage database operations (init, save, load, clear).
- I'll modify `js/app.js` to use the IndexedDB helper for fetching and storing Pokémon data.
- I'll ensure that if data in IndexedDB is invalid or missing, the app falls back to fetching from the API and repopulating the cache.
- The old localStorage cache key (`pokemonGeneratorCache_v5`) for Pokémon data will be removed upon successful migration to IndexedDB for existing users.
- Other localStorage usage (filters, shiny status, etc.) will remain unchanged for this iteration.
- I've thoroughly analyzed various scenarios including initial load, cache hits, cache clearing, and invalid cache handling.

author: huijinghei
body:
This is the preparation for https://github.com/coreos/bootupd/pull/855.

The main target for this PR is: "efi: rewrite `ensure_mounted_esp()`", but find there are much to update consequently.

---
efi: rewrite `ensure_mounted_esp()`

Split into 2 parts:
- `get_mounted_esp()` to get mounted point esp
- `mount_esp_device()` to mount the passed esp device, return
the mount point

Then in `ensure_mounted_esp()` call the above 2 functions:
firstly check if esp is already mounted, if not, mount the passed
esp device.

---
efi: update `install()` and `update()` according to split change

---
adopt_update: pass `RootContext` as parameter

---
efi: update `validate()` according to the split change

## Description
Added Integrity Checks for PSync and RSync flows in Trustpay. 
Why not for other flows as well?
The reason being, Trustpay doesnt send `amount` field in their response. Without getting to know the `amount`, we cannot perform integrity check. But they do send an `amount` field in Webhooks, so it will be checked upon receiving the webhooks payload. 

Also added a function which converts f64 to StringMajorUnit directly because there wasn't any function already which does it. We needed this function to convert the amount being received in f64 from Webhooks into StringMajorUnit which is required for the integrity check function.

Also added new enum variants in AttemptStatus and IntentStatus. In AttemptStatus added an enum variant "IntegrityFailure" and in IntentStatus added an enum variant "Conflicted".

body:
Consider the following signal declaration:
```
CM_ SG_ 2147548912 Foobar "Foo \"bar\"";
```

It has the word "bar" in quotation marks inside the comment string.
The current version of can-dbc fails to parse this.

This PR fixes this issue so that the comment gets parsed as `Foo \"bar\"` (_including_ the escape characters themselves!).

The fix is small, and unittests are included, so should hopefully be easy to accept. :)

body:
This pull request updates the `GitHubTeamManager` documentation to reflect changes in the application's functionality and configuration, particularly the transition from using the SCIM API to the External Groups API for GitHub Enterprise. It also updates configuration details to align with the new API usage.

### Updates to functionality:
* The application now fetches external groups using the GitHub External Groups API instead of the SCIM API, specifically for GitHub Enterprise EMU accounts. It creates and links GitHub Teams to these external groups and ignores groups if a team with the same name already exists. (`README.md`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c32e2fa7d8392591f0cb31d851fff5e7f9ab41f0451455849f0e1010e868fa90L3-R33) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L57-R59)

### Configuration changes:
* The structure of `appsettings.json` has been updated to group GitHub-related settings under a single `GitHub` object, simplifying configuration. author: kylesayrs
body:
# Summary
- Introduce Transform Args, Scheme, Config and Data as structures to define recipes to apply transforms 
- When compared to https://github.com/neuralmagic/compressed-tensors/pull/275, the requirement for `ModuleTarget`, and `TransformData` has been removed as well as the `transform_creation_args` and `call_args` fields
- Supports spinquant-like transform configs which target non-linear modules such as `q_attn` and `k_cache`

#### `TransformArgs`
- Arguments which define how and where a transform should be applied to a model

#### `TransformScheme`
- Scheme used to parameterize a particular transform type and specify how and where it should be applied to the model
- Includes a list of `TransformationArgs` onto which the transformation will be applied

#### `TransformConfig`
- Configuration of transforms to be applied to a model. This config is to be serialized within a model's `config.json` file
- The keys can be any arbitrary string and a TransformationScheme should be provided for each new transform type.
- Include preset configs for QUIP/QUIP# and Llama-SpinQuant

# Example:
```python
from compressed_tensors.transform import TransformArgs, TransformScheme, TransformsConfig

forward_args = TransformArgs(targets=["Linear"], location="input")  # non-mergable
inverse_args = TransformArgs(targets=["Linear"], location="weight_input", inverse=True)

scheme = TransformScheme(
    type="hadamard",
    apply=[forward_args, inverse_args],
    randomize_modules=True
)

config = TransformsConfig(transform_groups={"v_transform": scheme}
```

```
# [transform locations] and {quant locations}:
# input  <- {input @ [input]}
# weight <- {[weight_output] @ weight @ [weight_input]}
# output <- {input @ weight.T @ [output]}
```

author: onemorewe
body:
This commit introduces a suite of integration tests for the accounting ledger application.

Key features of the test suite:
-   JUnit 5 is used as the testing framework.
-   An `IntegrationTestBase` class provides utilities for:
    - Managing test-specific transaction CSV files (loaded from `src/test/resources`).
    - Simulating console input (`System.in`).
    - Capturing console output (`System.out`).
    - Resetting the `CsvTransactionRepository` singleton to ensure test isolation.
-   Test-specific application properties (`src/test/resources/application.properties`) are used to redirect the application to use a temporary transactions file (`target/test_transactions.csv`) during tests.

Integration tests cover the following scenarios:
-   **Adding a new transaction**: Verifies that you can navigate the menus, input transaction details, and that the transaction is persisted correctly to the CSV file.
-   **Displaying ledger entries**: Verifies that transactions from a pre-loaded CSV file are correctly displayed on the ledger screen.
-   **Month-to-Date Report**: Verifies that the MTD report correctly filters and displays transactions based on the current date at the time of test execution.
-   **Previous Month Report**: Verifies that the Previous Month report correctly filters and displays transactions based on the current date at the time of test execution.

These tests improve confidence in the application's core logic and data handling by simulating user interaction flows and validating both console output and data persistence.

author: hideoo
body:
#### Description

This PR is a follow-up to #3140.

~~This PR is a draft PR as I'd like to get some eyes on it with mutiple people testing it in multiple browsers during a Talking and Doc'ing session.~~

Turns out that the issue was not entirely fixed:

- Use Chrome or Safari
- Double click the last word (or single word for a heading with only 1 word) of a heading with a clickable anchor link
- Copy the selected text

The clipboard will contain an extra new line character at the end of the copied text.

- My [initial fix in Astro Docs](https://github.com/withastro/docs/pull/8015) was also not entirely correct as the issue only happens when the anchor link is after the heading, but on larger displays, in Astro Docs, the anchor link is currently before the heading. To reproduce the issue in Astro Docs, you need to resize the window to make the anchor link appear after the heading.
- My testing method was bad: I double clicked a word, copied it to my clipboard, pressed `Cmd + T` to open a new tab and focus the address bar, and pasted the text there. This is not a good test as the address bar will trim any trailing new line characters. To properly test this, I should have pasted the text in a text editor.

After quite a bit of trial and error, one of the solution I found was to change the `display` property of the link to `inline-flex` (`inline-block` does not work, don't ask me why) which should not have any side effects.

Reason: in 13.0, field default value had priority over data-for so an
issue was solved by b637a5e32f767b62736241042f88fa0cecf9f10b that if you
saved a form, the data-for would become the default for all the uses of
that form (so eg. a job position would be set for all job positions).

In 8d0a63f35519090a74fcefedf482fea5f6eedd97 the priority was changed so
data-for has higher priority than the default value, that made the
prior fix unnecessary (just a nice to have, to not save the data-for as
default that would be overridden by another data-for).

The fix was reintroduced by ca433f38dbfe379dc9e0b823c7862eaec1a7ed9d but
it removes default value if there is a data-for.

Fix: remove the filling and removing of value: the data-for is not shown
in the editor (allowing us to set default) but has the priority when
rendering the field in non-editable mode. This is mirroring what is
already done for data-fill-with.

Side note: this commit also remove useless data-fill-with="undefined"
attributes that are added when editing field. They shouldn't cause any
issue unless someone add a "undefined" field in the prefilled fields.
